solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Notice saying – 'Move up and down alternately'

blocks.note: to notice something is to see it
a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: A sign posted somewhere instructs people to bob up and down in turns.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash and quotation marks make 'saying' look like it introduces a quote; it is a noun, the proverb sense of SAW.
explanation.definitionFit: To seesaw is to rock alternately up and down, like children on a playground plank.

clue.text: A mixture of drugs and drink

blocks.note: first meaning: street slang for a combination of cocaine and heroin
second meaning: a cocktail of advocaat and lemonade

explanation.surface: A warning about combining narcotics with alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one dangerous combination; split it into two separate meanings. A snowball is a festive British cocktail of advocaat and lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word is slang for a cocaine-heroin combination and the name of a sweet Christmas cocktail.

clue.text: Not prepared in time to meet first of rocks in river

indicators.note: meeting means the two parts are joined end to end
only the opening letter of the next word is wanted
being in something means sitting inside it, so the river wraps around the rest

blocks.note: the Exe is a river in Devon; it wraps the rest
tempo is the time or speed of music
the opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone failed to get ready in time to see the first boulders in a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England; 'time' is musical speed, not the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Extempore speaking is done without preparation, off the cuff.

clue.text: Old artist almost flipped

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut
something flipped is turned over, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: Degas, the French painter, without his last letter

explanation.surface: An elderly painter has nearly toppled over.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgar Degas loses his final S, and what is left is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged is a synonym of old, describing someone advanced in years.

clue.text: Set off late

blocks.note: first meaning: left on a journey
second meaning: dead, as in 'the late king'

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests leaving behind schedule; 'late' is the euphemism for dead.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of leave on a journey and also a polite adjective for someone who has died.

clue.text: Find out more at court

blocks.note: extra means additional, more
CT is the standard abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A lawyer discovers further details while at a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find out more' looks like one phrase; the definition stops after 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract information is to draw it out or discover it, often with effort.

clue.text: Completely repaired leather around most of ancient garment

indicators.note: something repaired has been put back together, so the letters are reassembled
most of means all but the last letter is kept
around means wrapped about the outside of another part

blocks.note: the word leather rearranged, then split around the garment
a toga, the Roman robe, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone mended leather all the way round a Roman robe.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged leather becomes AL...ETHER with the shortened toga in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether is an adverb meaning entirely or in total.

clue.text: Including all books returned before volunteers left

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters run the other way
before means the parts are placed one ahead of the next

blocks.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
the TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Library books were brought back before the volunteer helpers went home.
explanation.walkthrough: OT reversed gives TO; the Territorial Army is the British army's part-time volunteer force.
explanation.definitionFit: A total figure is one that includes everything, the whole sum.

clue.text: Oddly deaf to academics over Kierkegaard's earliest material

indicators.note: oddly points to the letters in odd positions only
in a down entry, over means placed above the next part
the earliest letter of a name is its first

blocks.note: first and third letters
MAs are Masters of Arts, graduates
the philosopher's initial

explanation.surface: Strangely, scholars ignore the Danish philosopher's early writings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like the philosopher's work; it is fabric, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a reversible patterned fabric, originally from Damascus.

clue.text: Work on model's face

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means sitting on top of the next part

blocks.note: OP is short for opus, a work
to model is to pose for an artist

explanation.surface: An artist works on painting the face of a sitter.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S is 'is', joining wordplay to definition; 'face' is a verb, not a feature.
explanation.definitionFit: To face an opponent is to confront or stand against them, which is to oppose.

clue.text: He's not prepared to take marijuana there and then

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready or worked up, so the letters are rearranged
taking on something adds it at the end

blocks.note: the letters of these two words rearranged
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A man refuses to get ready to smoke cannabis immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's not prepared' reads like refusal; 'prepared' is the anagram signal working on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: On the spot is an idiom for immediately and at the place where something happens.

clue.text: Hottentot emblem featuring a symbol of spiritual significance

indicators.note: the phrase features the answer, carrying it inside its run of letters

blocks.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A tribal emblem from southern Africa bears a sacred sign.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the two words; the surface's tribal theme disguises that the answer belongs in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is a natural object or animal revered as an emblem of a clan, with sacred meaning.

clue.text: Fail in turning rabble against bishop

indicators.note: turning round means the letters are read backwards
against means placed right beside the next part

blocks.note: a mob is a disorderly crowd
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A crowd turns on a church leader and the effort fails.
explanation.definitionFit: To bomb is informal for to fail badly, as a show that flops.

clue.text: City's front line has exceptional goal sense

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter
exceptional means out of the ordinary, so the letters fall out of order
has means is followed by the next part

blocks.note: the opening letter
these nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A football club's forward line has a fine nose for goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Front line' and 'goal sense' sound like football talk; the city is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Los Angeles is a major city in California.

clue.text: Excellent reception

blocks.note: first meaning: of the highest quality
second meaning: in English primary schools

explanation.walkthrough: 'Excellent reception' sounds like a warm welcome or a good signal. Reception is the starting year of English primary school, at age four or five.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an adjective for top quality and, literally, the first class a child joins at school.

clue.text: Glorify Zion inordinately in story

indicators.note: inordinately suggests things out of order, so the letters are scrambled
in means placed inside the following word

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged; they go inside
a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: A tale that praises Zion to excess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In story' places the rearranged holy name inside the falsehood, not inside a narrative about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To lionize someone is to treat them as a celebrity, to praise and glorify them.

clue.text: Extremely tense before the king shows restraint

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outer letters
before means the parts run one after another in that order

blocks.note: first and last letters
taken as written
R is rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A very anxious monarch manages to hold himself back.
explanation.definitionFit: A tether is a rope or chain that restrains an animal, so it is a restraint.

clue.text: Undemanding church broadcast is a source of comfort

blocks.note: easy means not demanding
CH is the abbreviation for church
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: An easy-going church service on radio comforts its listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of comfort' suggests spiritual solace; it is a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair is a large, comfortable upholstered armchair.

clue.text: Magnificence of garden changed the centre of Thurso

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters take a new order
the centre of a word is its middle letters

blocks.note: the six letters rearranged
the two middle letters

explanation.surface: A splendid garden transformed the middle of a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Thurso is a town on the far north coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandeur is splendour and impressiveness, a synonym of magnificence.

clue.text: Thoroughly acquainted with poetry department's head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: verse is poetry
the opening letter

explanation.surface: The head of a poetry department knows the subject inside out.
explanation.definitionFit: To be versed in something is to be skilled or knowledgeable about it.

clue.text: Empty entirely to remove outside pressure

indicators.note: outside means wrapping round the next part

blocks.note: to delete is to remove
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: To drain something fully, take away the pressure around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remove outside pressure' reads as taking pressure off, but 'outside' is the instruction to wrap the verb round the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete is to use up or exhaust a supply, to empty it.

clue.text: A poet from Sweden writes about going west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means running right to left, backwards

blocks.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden
to pen is to write
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A Swedish poet writes about emigrating to America.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the last piece turns round. Edmund Spenser wrote The Faerie Queene.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was an Elizabethan English poet, so he is an example of a poet.

clue.text: Start to use torture on Taliban leader

indicators.note: torture twists and contorts, so the letters are wrenched into a new order
the leader of a word is its first letter
in a down entry, on means placed above the next part

blocks.note: the five letters rearranged
the opening letter

explanation.surface: An order to begin interrogating a Taliban commander harshly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Torture' looks like the verb of the surface's grim scene; it is the anagram signal acting on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out is a phrasal verb meaning to begin a journey or task.

clue.text: Washington to take a vote over strike

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned over means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state
to poll is to take a vote

explanation.surface: The US capital holds a ballot on industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' sounds like a walkout; it means hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallop is a heavy blow, and to wallop is to hit hard.

clue.text: Expect a social worker to be involved without interest

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a chunk is removed

blocks.note: the ant is a social insect that works in a colony
to participate is to take part
a part or share in something is an interest in it; this is removed

explanation.surface: A social worker is likely to take part even without being paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' is a crossword favourite for the ant, a colony insect. 'Interest' looks like money on a loan; here it is a share.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate is to look forward to or foresee, to expect something.

clue.text: Story heard about Rasmussen's original route

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling
about means going round the next piece
the original letter is the first one

blocks.note: a story is a tale, which sounds the same as another word
the initial

explanation.surface: A tale reportedly told of the path taken by the explorer Rasmussen.
explanation.walkthrough: T(R)AIL: the soundalike goes round the initial. Knud Rasmussen was a Danish polar explorer, which suits the route.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is a path or track, a route to follow.

clue.text: All the rage to embrace company image

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold inside one's arms, so one part goes within the other

blocks.note: something in is fashionable
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A fashionable firm adopts a new brand image.
explanation.walkthrough: I(CO)N: the fashionable word wraps the business abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a picture or representation, especially a religious one, so an image.

clue.text: Bit of theatre missing from dull religious ceremony

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a single letter, here its first
missing from means that letter is taken out of the next word

blocks.note: the opening letter
trite means stale and dull

explanation.surface: A dreary church service lacks any drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a formal ritual or ceremony, often of a religious kind.

clue.text: Wool producer, 50, hit by onset of arthritis

indicators.note: by means set next to, so the parts sit side by side
the onset of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
to lam is to beat or thrash
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A fifty-year-old sheep farmer is stricken with the first signs of arthritis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit by' reads as afflicted; here 'hit' is LAM and 'by' places it next to the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American animal kept for its wool and as a pack animal.

clue.text: Shed light upon girl without name found in summer in Paris

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is dropped
found in means placed inside the next word

blocks.note: été is French for summer; it goes round the outside
a girl's name
N is the abbreviation for name; it is removed

explanation.surface: An anonymous girl in Paris for the summer explains things.
explanation.walkthrough: Lucinda loses her N and goes inside the French word for summer.
explanation.definitionFit: To elucidate is to make clear or explain, to throw light on something.

clue.text: Spread over the Italian reporter's final column

indicators.note: spread over means laid across the outside of the next part
final means only the last letter is used

blocks.note: a paste is a spread for bread; it wraps the next piece
il is Italian for the
the last letter

explanation.surface: A journalist's last piece spreads across the Italian newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: P(IL)ASTE then R. 'Column' looks like a newspaper column; it is architectural.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilaster is a flat rectangular column projecting from a wall.

clue.text: Letters from Bogarde are reportedly more expensive

indicators.note: letters from a phrase are a run taken straight out of it

blocks.note: the end of the first word, all of the second and start of the third

explanation.surface: Fan mail from Dirk Bogarde is said to cost more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' tempts a soundalike reading; it only supplies its first letter to the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Dearer is the comparative of dear, which in British usage means costly.
